<Rep. Gerald E. Connolly>: Our government is a great experiment--the first government designed to be of, by, and for the American people. It is made up of dedicated public servants who take an oath to serve the American people, and support and defend the Constitution of the United States. They do not swear loyalty to a king or an emperor, or even the President or Congress, but to the Constitution. This oath is the foundation upon which every civil servant's career is built.
Yet President Trump has shown since the day he illegally fired 17 nonpartisan inspectors general that political loyalty is more important to him than the interests of the American people. Instead of supporting nonpartisan civil servants, he has worked to purge the federal government of these dedicated career professionals in favor of partisan hacks. Along with his chainsaw wielding billionaire donor, Elon Musk, President Trump is working to turn a nation of laws for the people into a nation of grift for the wealthy.
In an unprecedented arrangement, Trump has bestowed expansive, unlawful, and possibly unconstitutional authority on this unelected billionaire. Mr. Musk is redirecting billions of taxpayer dollars to fund his own financial interests while slashing federal government employees, programs, and services. At the same time, Mr. Musk remains in charge of a sprawling private sector business empire that continues to rely on billions of dollars in government funding and has been charged with managing his own conflicts of interest.
As of February 2025, Mr. Musk has been promised a combined total of at least $38 billion in contracts, loans, subsidies, and tax credits from federal and state governments. Mr. Musk continues to profit from taxpayer dollars and now finds himself in charge of determining which federal contracts the government will keep and which will be cut--an arrangement that runs afoul of the law and is a recipe for corruption.
Mr. Musk's space exploration company, SpaceX, and its satellite and telecommunications subsidiary, Starlink, have benefitted from a General Services Administration multiple award schedule contract for satellite services and equipment through which the companies have received $1.8 million from various federal agencies since 2021. At the Department of Transportation, Mr. Musk's DOGE operation has directed the firing of 400 employees at the Federal Aviation Administration, which just months earlier fined Mr. Musk's SpaceX company for disregarding license requirements for two of its launches. DOGE also fired 4% of the 800-person workforce at the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's, which has opened five investigations into Tesla, several of which concern life-threatening flaws with the car's ``self-driving'' mode, including unexpected braking, loss of steering control, and crashes. Elon Musk is circumventing federal ethics laws to avoid filing the public financial disclosures required of senior Administration officials, which further obscures the extent of his conflicts of interest.
This resolution of inquiry is simple. It would require the President to provide information about Musk's actual status within the federal government, any conflicts of interest Mr. Musk has related to his role in the federal government, and any federal contract involving a Musk-owned company or company on which he serves on the board of directors.
I did not introduce this resolution of inquiry lightly. In fact, Committee Democrats made numerous attempts to get this information before taking this step. We've sent 54 letters containing more than 400 requests. We've requested that Chairman Comer invite Mr. Musk to testify, and we even attempted to subpoena his appearance before this Committee to answer questions--an effort blocked by Committee Republicans who have always claimed to support transparency. At every attempt we have been rebuffed.
Given Mr. Musk's expansive influence in the Trump Administration, the American people have a right to know about his conflicts of interest. The American people have a right to know how the unelected billionaire bureaucrat taking a chainsaw to their government is enriching himself. The majority was gravely mistaken to vote against approving H. Res. 186.
Gerald E. Connolly,
Ranking Member.
